newsitem.title: UK: UK gas supply competition for homes a success - Ofgas.
newsitem.headline: UK gas supply competition for homes a success - Ofgas.

text.p: Industry regulator Ofgas said on Thursday that competition in Britain's domestic gas market had proved a success.
Director General of Gas Supply Clare Spottiswoode said in Offgas' 1996 report that the extension of competition from industry to homes had worked, despite a challenging timetable.
"Competition in supply, already established in the industrial and commercial market, was extended to the domestic market in April 1996, the target month agreed in December 1993," Spottiswoode said.

"And it works. What some said could not be done, and many more doubted could be done in the timetable we set ourselves, is now delivering the benefits of competition to a steadily increasing number of households."

She identified the implementation of the new Gas Act, the introduction of licences for companies serving the domestic market, the start of domestic competition and the operation of the Network Code as the year's biggest changes.

Ofgas said that when the initial phase of domestic competition started in Devon, Cornwall and Somerset on April 29 last year, 30,000 eligible customers out of a total of 500,000 switched suppliers on the first day. This could save between 10 and 20 percent of the standard British Gas tariff.

Complaints over doorstep selling led to Ofgas taking action against two companies, SWEB Gas and Eastern Natural Gas. As a result SWEB halted its sales campaign while Eastern tightened its code of conduct.
From October 1 TransCo, the pipeline arm of British Gas, opened up meter reading to competition and, by December, 23 different meter reading companies were registered with Ofgas.

Ofgas handled a record 9,287 complaints and enquiries about British Gas during 1996, up by 174 percent, although some of these may have resulted from customers contacting Ofgas instead of the Gas Consumer's Council.
